questions.question: Who emphasized the worship of God as Nirankar (Formless) in Punjab?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Baba Dayal Das.

  • Baba Dayal Das founded the Nirankari Movement and emphasized the worship of God as Nirankar (Formless).
  • Baba Ram Singh was the leader of the Kuka movement.
  • Maharaja Ranjit Singh was the first Maharaja of the Sikh Empire ('Sher-e-Punjab').

questions.question: The first session of All India Depressed Classes Congress was held at ______ in 1930.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nagpur.

The first session of the All India Depressed Classes Congress was held in Nagpur in 1930.

  • It was led by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
  • He also founded the Bahishkrit Hitkarini Sabha (Outcastes Welfare Association) in 1923.
  • The Poona Pact (1932) was a result of negotiations between Ambedkar and Gandhi.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Pandita Ramabai:
1. She founded the Arya Mahila Samaj to promote women's education and social reform.
2. She was the first woman to be awarded the titles Pandita and Sarasvati for her knowledge of Sanskrit.
3. She was the founder of the Depressed Class Mission in Mumbai in 1906.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

  • Statement 1 is correct: She founded the Arya Mahila Samaj to promote women's education and social reform.
  • Statement 2 is correct: She was the first woman awarded the titles 'Pandita' and 'Sarasvati'.
  • Statement 3 is incorrect: The Depressed Class Mission was founded by V.R. Shinde in 1906, not by Pandita Ramabai.

questions.question: In 1930, ______ led a satyagraha for the rights of untouchables' entry to the Kalaram temple at Nasik.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

  • In 1930, Ambedkar led the Kalaram Temple entry movement in Nashik.
  • In 1920, he began the weekly 'Mooknayak' (Leader of the Silent) in Mumbai.
  • His important writings include: 'The Annihilation of Caste', 'Who Were the Shudras', 'The Untouchables', and 'Riddles in Hinduism'.

questions.question: Which of the following was known as the forerunner of the Brahmo Samaj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Atmiya Sabha.

  • Atmiya Sabha was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1815.
  • It was the forerunner of the Brahmo Samaj (founded in 1828).
  • Brahmo Samaj split into two in 1866: Brahmo Samaj of India (Keshub Chandra Sen) and Adi Brahmo Samaj (Debendranath Tagore).

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs of Newspapers/Journals and their founders/editors:
1. Nibandhmala - Vishnushashti Chiplunkar
2. Prabhakar - Gopal Hari Deshmukh
3. Kesari - Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak
4. Pudhari - Swami Vivekananda
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Only three.

  • Pair 1 is correct: Nibandhmala was founded/edited by Vishnushashti Chiplunkar.
  • Pair 2 is correct: Prabhakar was edited by Gopal Hari Deshmukh.
  • Pair 3 is correct: Kesari was edited by Bal Gangadhar Tilak (1881).
  • Pair 4 is incorrect: Pudhari (Marathi daily, 1937) was not founded by Swami Vivekananda. He founded 'Udbodhan' (1899).

questions.question: The Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha was established at
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bombay.

The Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (Outcastes Welfare Association) was established by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in 1923 in Bombay.

  • Its aim was to promote education and socio-economic upliftment of depressed classes.
  • It also published the newspaper 'Mooknayak'.

questions.question: The Vidhava Vivaha Uttejaka Mandal (Society for Encouragement of Widow Marriage) was established in ______ in the second half of the nineteenth century.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bombay Presidency.

  • It was established by Vishnushastri Pandit in 1866 in Bombay Presidency.
  • The Hindu Widow Remarriage Act (1856) was passed by Lord Canning with the efforts of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.
  • Sati was abolished by William Bentinck in 1829 with Raja Ram Mohan Roy's efforts.

questions.question: The Begums of Bhopal founded a primary school for girls in the early twentieth century at
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Aligarh.

The Begums of Bhopal played a vital role in promoting education among Muslim women.

  • They founded a primary school for girls at Aligarh in the early 20th century.
  • Nawab Begum was the founding Chancellor of Aligarh Muslim University.

questions.question:
Match the following social reformers with the organizations they were associated with:
1. Dadoba Pandurang - Paramhansa Sabha
2. V R Shinde - Depressed Class Mission
3. Tulsi Ram - Radha Swami Satsang
4. G G Agarkar - Deccan Education Society
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1, 2, 3 and 4.

  • Paramhansa Sabha was founded by Dadoba Pandurang.
  • V.R. Shinde founded the Depressed Class Mission in Mumbai in 1906.
  • Radha Swami Satsang was founded by Tulsi Ram in 1861.
  • G.G. Agarkar was a co-founder of the Deccan Education Society (1884).

questions.question: Who among the following wrote the Brahmo Covenant, which was a statement of the creed of the Brahmo Samaj and made a list of the duties and obligations of its members?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Debendranath Tagore.

  • Debendranath Tagore (father of Rabindranath Tagore) wrote the Brahmo Covenant in 1848.
  • He founded the Tattvabodhini Sabha in 1839 and joined Brahmo Samaj in 1842.
  • He founded Shantiniketan ('Abode of Peace') in 1863.

questions.question: Who among the following was NOT a Nayanar saint?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Andal.

The Nayanars were a group of 63 poet-saints in Tamil Nadu (6th to 8th centuries CE) devoted to Lord Shiva.

  • Famous Nayanars include Sundarar, Appar, and Sambandar.
  • Andal was an Alvar (not a Nayanar). The Alvars were devotees of Vishnu.
  • The Bhakti movement was influenced by both Nayanars and Alvars.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a correct match of Dargah and its respective location?
questions.option_2: Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki Dargah - Delhi
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya Dargah - Agra.

  • Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya's Dargah is located in Delhi (Nizamuddin West), not Agra.
  • Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki's Dargah is in Delhi.
  • Haji Ali Dargah is in Mumbai.
  • Shaikh Muinuddin Sijzi (Chishti) Dargah is in Ajmer (Ajmer Sharif).

questions.question: Who among the following is known as the 'father of Muslim renaissance' in Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nawab Abdul Latif Khan.

  • Nawab Abdul Latif Khan is known as the 'father of Muslim renaissance' in Bengal.
  • His title 'Nawab' was awarded by the British in 1880.
  • He was one of the first Muslims in 19th century India to embrace modernization.

questions.question: Who was the first woman to be the president of the Indian National Congress?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Annie Besant.

Annie Besant became the president of the Indian National Congress in 1917 (Calcutta session).

  • She was a British-born social reformer and theosophist.
  • She also founded the Home Rule League in 1916.
  • Sarojini Naidu became the first Indian woman president of INC in 1925.

questions.question: With whose participation did the Anushilan group join forces when the Bengal Congress broke up into two factions after the death of C.R. Das?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is J.M. Sengupta.

After Chittaranjan Das's death in 1925, the Bengal Congress split into moderates and radicals.

  • The radical faction was led by J.M. Sengupta.
  • The Anushilan Samiti aligned with Sengupta's more aggressive nationalist stance.
  • Sengupta was a close associate of C.R. Das.

questions.question:
Consider the following sessions of the Indian National Congress and their Presidents:
1. Bombay, 1885 - W.C. Banerjee
2. Madras, 1887 - Badruddin Tyabji
3. Belgaum, 1924 - ?
4. Lahore, 1929 - Jawaharlal Nehru
Who presided over the Belgaum Session of 1924?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

The 39th session of INC at Belgaum was held on December 26, 1924.

  • Mahatma Gandhi presided over the Belgaum session (1924).
  • Bombay, 1885 (W.C. Banerjee) - First session
  • Madras, 1887 (Badruddin Tyabji) - First Muslim President
  • Lahore, 1929 (Jawaharlal Nehru) - Poorna Swaraj resolution

questions.question: Where was the 1912 session of the India National Congress held in Bihar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bankipore.

The 27th session of the Indian National Congress in 1912 was presided over by Raghunath Narasinha Mudholkar and was held at Bankipore (now part of Patna, Bihar).

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to become the Governor-General of independent India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is C. Rajagopalachari.

  • C. Rajagopalachari served as the Governor-General of India from June 1948 to January 1950.
  • Lord Mountbatten was the first Governor-General of independent India but was British, not Indian.
  • After India became a republic in 1950, Dr. Rajendra Prasad became the first President.

questions.question: The famous 'Nehru Report' (1928) was prepared by a committee headed by Motilal Nehru. Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Nehru Report?
questions.option_4: Federal structure with residuary powers with provinces
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Separate electorates for minorities.

The Nehru Report (1928) recommended Dominion status (not complete independence), a Bill of Rights, and a federal structure with residuary powers with provinces. However, it rejected separate electorates for minorities and recommended joint electorates with reserved seats.

questions.question: The famous 'August Offer' of 1940 was issued by which Viceroy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Linlithgow.

The August Offer of 1940 was issued by Viceroy Lord Linlithgow. It promised Dominion status in the unspecified future and expansion of the Viceroy's Executive Council to include more Indians. It was rejected by the Congress as it did not guarantee complete independence.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first Indian woman to preside over the Indian National Congress session?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Annie Besant.

Annie Besant was the first woman to preside over the Indian National Congress session in 1917 (Calcutta session). Though she was British-born, she is considered the first woman president of INC.

  • Sarojini Naidu became the first Indian woman president of INC in 1925 (Kanpur session).
  • Indira Gandhi never served as INC president while in office.

questions.question: The first session of the Indian National Congress (1885) was held in Bombay under the presidentship of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is W.C. Bonnerjee.

The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay in December 1885.

  • President: W.C. Bonnerjee (Wyomesh Chandra Banerjee)
  • Founder: Allan Octavian Hume
  • Attendees: 72 delegates from across India.

questions.question: The 'Poorna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) resolution was passed at the Lahore session of the Indian National Congress in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1929.

The Lahore session of 1929 was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru.

  • The 'Poorna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) resolution was passed on December 19, 1929.
  • January 26, 1930, was celebrated as the first Independence Day.
  • The Indian tricolor flag was hoisted on the banks of the Ravi River.

questions.question: The 'Surat Split' of the Indian National Congress took place in the year:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1907.

The Surat Split occurred in December 1907 at the Surat session of INC.

  • The split was between Moderates (led by Gopal Krishna Gokhale) and Extremists (led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, Lala Lajpat Rai).
  • The issue was over the election of the President and Swadeshi movement tactics.
  • The Congress reunited in 1916 at the Lucknow session.
